headline: Ways community preservation funds and affordable housing trusts can work together, presented by Mass Housing Partnership.
summary: The talk covered the Community Preservation Act and the trust law, and advised using grant agreements whenever funds are given out. Norwell and Beverly were given as examples of towns where a trust and a community preservation committee both paid for housing. The committee also voted to take back $60,000 from Ascentria and $76,679 from the Olympia Theater project. Olympia Theater is expected to apply again in round three.
decisions: Approved taking back $60,000 from Ascentria and placing it in the budget reserve.
Approved taking back $76,679 from the Olympia Theater project.
discussion: Percentage-based funding: The presenter said Cambridge moves 80% of its CPA funds to its trust and Somerville about 45%. The state coalition advised against a fixed percentage so there is room for emergencies.
Trust funding sources: Since the ordinance passed in May 2023, the trust has received $181,000 from inclusionary zoning. The trust said that is not its most reliable source of funds.

Accessible unit requirements: The trust said its requests call for at least 10% of units in a project to be fully accessible, and that the affordability lasts 30 years. Members asked for more on accessibility, and the trust will discuss accessible housing at its December 16th meeting.

Olympia Theater funding: The project will use $84,202.50 of its round two award for structural drawing, engineering, and wall restoration. Members questioned whether the award amounts add up, and staff said they would double-check.

Project updates and schedule: The committee asked for a written status update on each project at every meeting, and 10 projects still need contracts. Pre-applications are due December 2nd, and full applications are due January 7th.
